preamble: Centralization of the near-close near-front [ɪ] to the mid central [ə]. In the English weak vowel merger, unstressed [ɪ] as in roses and Lenin falls together with the schwa of Rosa's and Lennon in most Australian, New Zealand, North American and Irish accents and in 21st-century Southern British speech; traditional RP keeps the two apart.

examples.from: roses with final-syllable [ɪ] (speakers without the merger, traditional RP)
examples.to: /ˈroʊzəz/, listed with Rosa's as a merged pair
examples.note: Unstressed [ɪ] merges with schwa in most Australian, New Zealand, North American and Irish accents and in 21st-century Southern British speech. Some merged speakers, such as General American ones, still keep roses apart from Rosa's because of the morpheme break in Rosa's.
